notes:
Deeper history, and the theme graph where you can find it.

History past 30 days: dashy used to forget daily activity after a month, so
the theme graph and effort matrix could never look further back than that. A
new "dashy history-backfill" command rebuilds the missing days from your git
commits, letting both surfaces show a project from its first commit rather
than only its last month.

Theme lineage on the Overview: the graph of how one idea led to another now
appears on each project's Overview page, instead of sitting two clicks away
behind the effort matrix.

Pick any date range: the lineage graph gains 180-day and 365-day lookbacks,
an "All" option covering a project's whole recorded history, and start and
end date pickers for anything in between. Leave the end date blank and it
means today.

Group by day, week, or month: connections between themes get harder to see
the longer the window, because effort keeps accumulating while same-day
overlap does not. Grouping by week or month brings that structure back
without changing how large any theme is.

Also in this release: the lineage detail panel now answers from whatever
range and grouping you are actually viewing, rather than always falling back
to the last 30 days.
